subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should canonical OpenAI usage status read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles at runtime, or should affected users be required to run `openclaw doctor --fix` first?
rationale: Repository policy normally keeps legacy `openai-codex` state in doctor/migration paths, while this PR deliberately adds a runtime compatibility bridge for a shipped upgrade edge.

options.title: Approve the usage-only bridge
options.body: Accept the runtime fallback only for provider-usage status so legacy stored OAuth/token profiles keep producing canonical OpenAI quota output before doctor migration.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Close or pause the PR and require users with legacy profile ids to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before usage status reads those credentials.

options.title: Request a narrower refreshed patch
options.body: Ask for a rebase plus explicit comments/tests that separate this stored-profile bridge from the synthetic Codex app-server route.

recommendation.title: Approve the usage-only bridge
recommendation.body: Accept the runtime fallback only for provider-usage status so legacy stored OAuth/token profiles keep producing canonical OpenAI quota output before doctor migration.

likelyOwner.reason: The OpenAI provider identity migration and provider-usage auth history point to this owner for the legacy-runtime compatibility decision.
